topic_and_scope: Evaluation of antidiabetic and anti-obesity pharmacotherapies for MASLD/MASH in patients with T2DM and advanced liver disease (fibrosis/cirrhosis), focusing on safety, efficacy, mechanisms, and trial design to guide treatment in compensated and decompensated states.
main_themes: Safety and efficacy of existing and emerging antidiabetic medications in MASLD-related cirrhosis, with emphasis on compensated vs decompensated disease and pharmacokinetic considerations.

Promise and uncertainty of novel therapies (GLP-1RAs, GLP-1R/GCGR and GIP/GLP-1 co-agonists, FGF/FGF19 analogs, PPAR modulators, galectin-3 inhibitors) for reducing hepatic fat, inflammation, fibrosis, and achieving recompensation.

Need for robust, stage-specific clinical trials with cirrhosis-relevant endpoints, standardized non-invasive biomarkers, safety signals, and implementation considerations including cost-effectiveness and HCC surveillance.
main_findings: Several regimens (metformin, SGLT-2 inhibitors, GLP-1RAs) show potential for glycemic control and weight management in T2DM with compensated cirrhosis and MASLD, and may confer MASLD-related benefits; safety and efficacy data in decompensated cirrhosis remain limited.

Emerging dual/triple agonists (tirzepatide; survodutide, cotadutide, efinopegdutide, pemvidutide, mazdutide; retatrutide) and FGF/Galectin-3/PPAR pathways demonstrate impressive effects on liver fat, inflammation, and fibrosis in MASLD/MASH contexts, but evidence in established cirrhosis is scarce and most trials exclude decompensated patients.

key_gaps.description: Limited long-term safety and efficacy data for newer antidiabetic/anti-obesity drugs in cirrhosis, particularly decompensated cirrhosis, with unclear risk–benefit profiles and potential drug–drug interactions.

Need for high-quality, large-scale trials with cirrhosis-specific endpoints (MASH resolution without fibrosis progression, fibrosis stage change, recompensation, HVPG, HCC incidence) and cost-effectiveness analyses across diverse etiologies and Child–Pugh classes.

future_directions.title: Perform large, randomized head-to-head trials comparing GLP-1RAs, SGLT-2 inhibitors, and DPP-4 inhibitors in MASLD-related cirrhosis (F2–F4).
future_directions.rationale: This will establish comparative safety and efficacy profiles across compensated and decompensated states, with standardized endpoints including liver fat content (MRI-PDFF), fibrosis markers (FIB-4, ELF), liver stiffness, and decompensation events. Trials should stratify by etiology (MASLD vs ALD vs viral), baseline glycemic control, and Child–Pugh class, and incorporate pharmacokinetic assessments to inform dosing in cirrhosis. Outcomes should include progression to decompensation, hospitalization rates, liver-related and all-cause mortality, and HCC incidence over long-term follow-up.

future_directions.title: Investigate tirzepatide and other GIP/GLP-1 co-agonists specifically in MASLD/MASH patients with cirrhosis (F2–F4) and assess recompensation potential.
future_directions.rationale: Early data suggest superior glycemic and weight outcomes with tirzepatide and favorable effects on liver fat. Trials should enroll participants with biopsy- or imaging-proven MASLD/MASH and cirrhosis, include serial liver biopsies or validated non-invasive endpoints, and track fibrosis stage, MASH activity, liver-related events, and survival. Mechanistic studies should evaluate insulin sensitivity, adipose-liver crosstalk, and inflammatory pathways to identify predictors of response.

future_directions.title: Assess dual GLP-1R/GCGR agonists (survodutide, cotadutide, efinopegdutide, pemvidutide, mazdutide) in cirrhosis (F2–F4) with rigorous safety monitoring.
future_directions.rationale: These agents show significant weight loss and metabolic benefits with potential antifibrotic effects in MASLD; however, data in cirrhosis are sparse. Phase II/III trials should evaluate fibrosis outcomes (at least one-stage improvement without MASH worsening), liver fat reduction, portal hypertension indicators, and hepatic or systemic adverse events in decompensated patients. PK analyses across Child–Pugh categories and interactions with standard cirrhosis therapies are essential.

future_directions.title: Explore THR-β agonist resmetirom and FGF analogs (Aldafermin, efruxifermin, pegozafermin, pegbelfermin) in compensated and decompensated MASLD/MASH cirrhosis.
future_directions.rationale: These agents target lipotoxicity, steatosis, and fibrosis via distinct metabolic pathways. Trials should assess fibrosis endpoints, recompensation rates, HCC surveillance implications, and safety in decompensated cirrhosis. Long-term follow-up is needed to determine sustained histological and clinical benefits and to monitor potential interactions with other metabolic medications.

future_directions.title: Evaluate galectin-3 inhibitors and CCR2/CCR5 antagonists in MASLD-related cirrhosis for portal hypertension and fibrosis progression.
future_directions.rationale: Belapectin and related agents have shown signals for reducing HVPG and variceal risk in NASH cirrhosis, but phase III results are mixed or inconclusive. Focused trials should include compensated and decompensated cohorts, standardized HVPG and non-invasive fibrosis markers, and endpoints on variceal development, portal hypertension complications, and survival to clarify therapeutic value.

future_directions.title: Develop and test combination regimens (eg, GLP-1RA + FXR agonist + ACC inhibitor) in compensated MASLD-related cirrhosis.
future_directions.rationale: Combination therapies may yield synergistic antifibrotic and metabolic effects while allowing lower doses to reduce adverse events. Randomized trials should evaluate MASLD activity scores, fibrosis progression, liver fat reduction, and safety signals. Stratification by fibrosis stage and presence of diabetes will help identify subgroups with the greatest benefit.

future_directions.title: Implement pragmatic, multicenter trials and real-world studies to assess cost-effectiveness, health care utilization, and HCC surveillance impact of these therapies in cirrhotic populations.
future_directions.rationale: Cost-effectiveness and real-world adherence influence translation into practice. Studies should collect data on hospitalization rates, liver-related events, surveillance for HCC, quality of life, and healthcare costs across diverse health systems and etiologies. This will inform policy decisions and guideline development for treating MASLD/MASH-related cirrhosis with metabolic drugs.

future_directions.title: Standardize and validate cirrhosis-specific endpoints and non-invasive biomarkers for fibrosis and recompensation in trials of metabolic drugs.
future_directions.rationale: Current endpoints vary across studies, limiting cross-trial comparisons. A consensus set of endpoints, including non-invasive scores, imaging biomarkers, HVPG where feasible, and histologic correlates, is needed to reliably assess disease modification and to accelerate regulatory approval and clinical adoption in MASLD/MASH-related cirrhosis.
